_about: Local emergency and urgent-care configuration. Every entry traces to a Singapore government or public-healthcare source. Deliberately contains NO blood-pressure numbers: MOH's own high blood pressure page states no numeric threshold, so this app must not invent one. See docs/content-provenance.md.
_review_note: team_checked means a team member read the source and recorded it. It does NOT mean a clinician reviewed it. Clinician review is outstanding and is recorded as such in the trace page.
what_to_say: Say exactly where you are, including the block and unit number, or the nearest landmark.
Say what is happening and when it started.
Say how old the person is and what long-term medicines they take.
Stay on the line and follow the instructions you are given.

other_routes.label: Non-emergency ambulance
other_routes.note: SCDF has stated this hotline ceases from 1 January 2027. Confirm before relying on it.

other_routes.label: Emergency SMS
other_routes.note: For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have speech difficulty. The sender provides details by text.

other_routes.label: NurseFirst helpline
other_routes.note: Staffed by emergency-trained nurses who advise on the right care option. When a 995 call is assessed as not life-threatening it may be transferred here. It does not replace 995 if the person gets worse.

also: For a condition that is not an emergency, a GP or polyclinic is the usual route.
MOH advises bringing identification, medical documents, and a list of your medicines with doses.
If you are not sure whether it is an emergency, it is reasonable to call and ask.
warning: This app cannot assess how serious a situation is, and cannot contact anyone for you. The numbers above come from published Singapore sources; always check them yourself if you are relying on them in an emergency.
